newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HUNDLEY POWERS METS PAST REDS WITH TWO HOMERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HUNDLEY POWERS METS PAST REDS WITH TWO HOMERS.

text.p: Todd Hundley belted a pair of two-run homers and John Olerud added two RBI doubles to power the New York Mets to a 10-2 rout of the slumping Cincinnati Reds on Wednesday.

Hundley hit the first pitch he saw from Mike Morgan in the first inning over the right-field wall to give the Mets a 2-1 lead. In the sixth, he smacked a 3-0 offering from Kevin Jarvis down the right-field line for his fifth homer of the season to cap the scoring.
"I'm paid to drive in runs," Hundley said. "I was looking for some strikes and I got them, and I was able to hit them."
Edgardo Alfonso had two hits and scored twice and Bernard Gilkey doubled in a run for New York, which banged out 14 hits off five Cincinnati pitchers.
Mark Clark (2-1) allowed two runs and seven hits over seven innings to pick up the victory. Morgan (0-2) was tagged for six runs and seven hits over three innings for the loss.
Deion Sanders had three hits, scored a run and drove in another for Cincinnati, which has dropped four in a row and eight of nine.
In San Francisco, Bill Mueller's one-out single in the bottom of the ninth scored pinch-runner Dante Powell with the winning run as the Giants edged the Atlanta Braves 4-3.
Mueller laced an 0-1 pitch off reliever Alan Embree (1-1) to right field and Powell slid around the tag of Atlanta catcher Javy Lopez for the winning run.
Doug Henry (2-0) pitched a scoreless ninth to pick up the win for San Francisco.
Barry Bonds hit an inside-the-park three-run homer for the Giants, going over the 1,000-RBI mark for his career.
At Colorado, Walt Weiss's two-run triple broke a sixth-inning tie as the Rockies beat Kevin Brown and the Florida Marlins 7-3.
Andres Galarraga and pitcher Jamey Wright each added two hits and two RBI for Colorado, which has gone 12-3 since losing their first two games of the season.
Brown (2-1) entered the game with a league-leading 0.96 ERA, but surrendered five runs and 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings. The loss was just his second in 14 starts since last August 8.
Wright (3-1) allowed three runs and 10 hits over seven innings for the win.
In Montreal, Henry Rodriguez snapped a tie with an RBI double in the fifth inning as the Expos nipped the floundering Chicago Cubs 4-3.

After both teams scored three runs in the fourth, David Segui led off the fifth with a double off Terry Mulholland (0-3). He took third on a groundout and scored the winning run on Rodriguez's double to right field.
Jim Bullinger (1-3) got the win over his former team, allowing three runs and three hits over five innings. Lee Smith worked the ninth for his 475th career save.
In Pittsburgh, Mark Johnson's single with two outs in the bottom of the eighth inning scored Jermaine Allensworth from second and lifted the Pirates to a 3-2 victory over the Philadelphia Phillies.
The Pirates had tied the game 2-2 in the seventh when Jose Guillen drove in Kevin Elster with a sacrifice fly.

Ricardo Rincon (2-1) picked up the win after striking out Gregg Jefferies with two men on and two out in the eighth. He fanned two more batters in the ninth. Jerry Spradlin (0-1) suffered the loss in relief of Calvin Maduro.
In Los Angeles, Raul Mondesi drove in the go-ahead run with an eighth-inning single as the Dodgers snapped a three-game slide with a 2-1 win over the St Louis Cardinals.
Mark Petkovsek (2-3) loaded the bases in the eighth before giving up Mondesi's single that brought home Greg Gagne, who had doubled to extend his hitting streak to nine games.
Mark Guthrie (1-0) hurled 1 1/3 hitless innings in relief of Ramon Martinez for the win. Martinez allowed just two hits, including Ray Lankord's home run in the first inning.
Lankford had two hits. The rest of the Cardinals combined to go 1-for-26.
In San Diego, Jeff Bagwell's three-run homer snapped a tie and triggered a five-run sixth inning as the Houston Astros pounded the Padres 11-7.
Bagwell went 3-for-5 with four RBI and Brad Ausmus added three hits and three RBI for the Astros, who piled up a season-high 18 hits for their fourth win in a row.
Ramon Garcia (2-0) allowed one run and four hits over 3-2/3 innings in relief off starter Mike Hampton for the win. Loser Tim Worrell (1-3) gave up four runs and four hits in just 1-1/3 innings.
